newsitem.title: USA: Sun-Diamond convicted over gifts to ex-USDA chief.
newsitem.headline: Sun-Diamond convicted over gifts to ex-USDA chief.

text.p: Sun-Diamond Growers of California, the nation's largest fruit cooperative, was convicted Tuesday of illegally giving gifts and favours to former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy in 1993 and 1994.

The agricultural concern was also convicted on charges that it took part in a scheme to funnel illegal campaign contributions to Espy's brother Henry and was found guilty on two charges of wire fraud.

Sun-Diamond, whose affiliates include Sun Maid raisins, Sunsweet prunes and Diamond Walnut -- had been charged with violating nine criminal counts involving illegal gratuities and illegal campaign contributions.

After deliberating for 9-1/2 hours over two days a jury found Sun-Diamond not guilty of only one of the counts, which alleged that the cooperative had paid transportation costs for Espy's girlfriend to accompany him to a conference in Greece.
The Sun-Diamond trial was the first case to come to court as the result of the government's two-year special investigation of Espy led by Independent Counsel Donald Smaltz.

So far the investigation has resulted in five sets of criminal indictments and charges being brought against more than a dozen individuals and concerns, including the Washington lobbyist for the huge Arkansas-based chicken processor Tyson Foods, whose chairman has long had close ties to President Clinton when was former governor of Arkansas.
